What a First OWI Charge Puts at Risk in Davenport

A first-offense OWI in Iowa is a serious criminal charge. It carries real penalties — fines, a license suspension, and a potential jail sentence. Many people assume that a first offense results in a light outcome. That is not always true.

In Iowa, a first-offense OWI is classified as a Serious Misdemeanor under Iowa Code § 321J.2, carrying a mandatory minimum of 48 hours in jail (up to 1 year) and fines ranging from $625 to $1,250.

Administratively, the Iowa Department of Transportation revokes driving privileges for 180 days if a driver fails a chemical test, or for 1 year if they refuse testing under Iowa Code § 321J.9.

Moreover, offenders are required to complete a substance abuse evaluation, a court-approved Drinking Driver Course, and pay a $200 civil penalty to reinstate their license.

To maintain restricted driving privileges with an Ignition Interlock Device, drivers also need to file SR-22 proof of high-risk insurance for 2 years.

Without an experienced first-offense OWI defense lawyer, Davenport prosecutors move forward with whatever evidence they have. They are not looking out for you. Chemical test results can have flaws. Traffic stops can be unlawful. These are real defense angles — but only if someone acts on them now.

At Henkels & Baker, PC, we look closely at every detail of your case. We review the stop, the arrest, and the test results. If something was done wrong, we work to identify it. We also explore options like reduced charges or alternative sentencing when those paths make sense.

Key Facts About a First-Offense OWI in Iowa

  • A first-offense OWI is a Serious Misdemeanor under Iowa Code § 321J.2.

  • Penalties include a 48-hour to 1-year jail term and fines of $625 to $1,250.

  • License revocation runs 180 days for a failed test, or 1 year for a refusal.

  • A substance abuse evaluation and Drinking Driver Course are required.

  • Standard Iowa OWI convictions cannot be expunged, with a rare exception for a deferred judgment.

Your First OWI Case in Iowa: Step by Step

In Iowa, a first-offense OWI (operating while intoxicated) case moves through several clear stages under Iowa Code Chapter 321J, which governs impaired driving offenses. Knowing what comes next helps you feel less anxious and more in control.

  • Step 1: Initial Consultation: You share the facts — where you were stopped, what the officer said, and what tests were given. The goal is to get a full picture of what happened.

  • Step 2: Document Review: Your lawyer pulls the police report, dashcam or bodycam footage, and any chemical test results. A breath test can be challenged if the machine was not properly maintained.

  • Step 3: Building a Strategy: Iowa courts handle first-offense OWI cases differently from repeat offenses. Potential outcomes may include reduced charges, a deferred judgment, or a plea that limits long-term damage to your record.

  • Step 4: Court Appearances: Your lawyer goes to court with you through arraignment, pretrial hearings, and — if needed — trial. Most first-offense cases in Iowa are resolved before trial.

  • Step 5: License and Administrative Issues: Your criminal case and your license status run on separate tracks in Iowa, handled through a separate process with the Iowa Department of Transportation.

  • Step 6: Resolution: Most first-offense OWI cases end in one of three ways: a dismissed charge, a reduced charge, or a conviction with a defined penalty.

Our goal is to help you move through each stage with a clear head and a real plan.

A first OWI charge in Davenport does not have to define your future. The outcome may be influenced by how quickly you act and how well your case is handled from the start. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we understand what is at stake — your license, your job, and your record.

We are here to help you move forward with a clear head and a real plan.

Scott County Courts Move Fast

Scott County courts move fast. The sooner you have a first-offense OWI defense lawyer in Davenport reviewing your case, the more options you may have available to you.

Contact us and schedule a free initial consultation.

1. Can I still drive while my OWI case is pending in Iowa?

    2. You may be eligible for a temporary restricted license during your case, depending on your situation. This allows limited driving — such as to work or medical appointments — but requires meeting certain conditions set by the Iowa DOT.

  2. Will an OWI conviction show up on my background check?

    3. Yes, an OWI conviction in Iowa becomes part of your criminal record and may appear in background checks run by employers or landlords. A first-offense OWI defense lawyer in Davenport may be able to help you pursue options that avoid a permanent conviction on your record.

  3. What happens if I missed the deadline to request a license hearing?

    4. If you did not act within the required window, your license may be revoked by default — but other options may still exist. Speaking with an OWI defense lawyer in Davenport right away can help you understand what steps remain open to you.

  4. Does a first OWI offense in Iowa stay on my record forever?

    5. In Iowa, standard Operating While Intoxicated (OWI) convictions cannot be expunged, with a rare exception for first-time offenders who received a deferred judgment. Pursuing a strong defense from the start is often better to protect your future.
